claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first question:

**How old is your child (or oldest child if you have multiple)?**

Please let me know:
- The age of the child (or children) you're claiming for
- You can tell me all their ages if you have multiple children

Once I understand the age(s), I can guide you through the rest of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he automatically falls into the qualifying age category. Now let me proceed with the next check in the eligibility process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old, I assume he's not in paid work. Could you confirm that Alex is not working 24+ hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he's not working at all - he's just in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex is not working at all and is in primary school. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

In other words, is Alex receiving any of these benefits directly in his own name, or is he not receiving any of these?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not receiving any of those benefits. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check on apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship program?**

Since Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, I would assume he's not in any apprenticeship. Could you confirm that Alex is not currently in an apprenticeship of any kind?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! At 8 years old, Alex is definitely not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important part of the eligibility assessment.

**Where do you normally live?**

Here are the main paths that could make you eligible:

1. **Normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward option
2. **EU Settlement Scheme** - If you have settled or pre-settled status
3. **Crown servant abroad** - If you work abroad for the UK government
4. **Other special circumstances** - Various other criteria apply

Could you tell me: Do you normally live in the UK, or is your situation different (e.g., EU Settlement Scheme status, living abroad, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK in Manchester with Alex. That means you meet the residency requirements. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. This means you either:

1. **Live with the child** - which you do (you mentioned Alex lives with you at home)
2. OR contribute to their upkeep
3. OR pay maintenance under a court order

Since you've already told me that Alex lives with you at home in Manchester, you clearly meet the responsibility requirement. Let me proceed.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check:

**Is there anyone else (such as Alex's other parent, a relative, or someone else) who is also claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or who might also be eligible to claim?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- A grandparent
- Another guardian

Could you let me know if anyone else is claiming or could claim Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! So you're the only one claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
- Living at home with you normally?
- In hospital?
- In care?
- Fostered?

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex is living at home with you normally. Can you confirm that?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or fostered or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is living at home with you normally. Let me proceed with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! I just need to check one more thing:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for Alex's accommodation and upkeep yourself, or is the council paying for any part of it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm paying for everything myself for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're paying for everything yourself, and the council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. That means you've passed all the eligibility checks!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I'm pleased to inform you that **you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**.

## Summary of Your Eligibility

You meet all the requirements for Child Benefit:

✅ **Child's age**: Alex is 8 years old (under 16)  
✅ **Child's work status**: Not working full-time (not working at all)  
✅ **Benefits**: Alex is not receiving qualifying benefits in his own right  
✅ **Apprenticeship**: Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✅ **Residency**: You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ **Responsibility**: You live with Alex and are responsible for him  
✅ **No other claimants**: Only you are claiming for Alex  
✅ **Child's living situation**: Living at home with you normally  
✅ **Council funding**: The council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance  

## Next Steps

To claim Child Benefit for Alex, you need to:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, there may be a tax charge on the benefit

For more information and to apply, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations! Is there anything else you'd like to know about the Child Benefit claim?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Your eligibility has been confirmed in the system. You're all set to move forward with your Child Benefit claim for Alex. Good luck with your application!
